$help: Motor test configuration for the Raspberry Pi 4 ('nike') L298N 4-wheel chassis.
Anything here can also be overridden per run with CLI flags (run --help).
Generate a fresh copy of the effective config with --print-config / --write-config.
PIN MAP — verified free with `gpioinfo` + /sys/kernel/debug/pinctrl on this board:
left  en=12 (pin 32)  in1=17 (pin 11)  in2=27 (pin 13)   -> L298N ENA / IN1 / IN2
right en=13 (pin 33)  in3=22 (pin 15)  in4=23 (pin 16)   -> L298N ENB / IN3 / IN4
REFUSED by the script (reserved by configuration, not by a live claim):
GPIO14/15 = serial console. serial0 resolves to the mini-UART ttyS0 on these pins
(console=ttyS0,115200), and its pin mux is set by the firmware, so no
runtime check can see the conflict.
WARNED about: GPIO2/3 (I2C1), GPIO4 (GPCLK0/1-Wire), GPIO7-11 (SPI0), GPIO18-21 (PCM/I2S).
DO NOT CONFUSE THE CHIPS. gpiochip0 (pinctrl-bcm2711) is the 40-pin header. gpiochip1
(raspberrypi-exp-gpio) is the firmware expander, whose lines 5/6 are CAM_GPIO (camera
rail) and SD_PWR_ON (microSD power). Header GPIO5/GPIO6 are ordinary free pins; the
expander's are load-bearing. The script picks the SoC chip automatically — do not set
